newsitem.title: USA: US railroad administration issues safety directive.
newsitem.headline: US railroad administration issues safety directive.

text.p: The Federal Railroad Administration on Thursday directed U.S. railroads to review their safety programs for operational tests and inspections.
The FRA also directed railroads to follow new procedures in non-signaled areas.
The directive is based on preliminary findings of investigations into two train accidents earlier this month, the FRA said in statement.

After the rear-end collision between two CSX freight trains in West Virginia on June 7, the FRA concluded that each railroad should review its program of operational tests and inspections to ensure that they are carried out in accordance with requirements.
The railroads must inform the FRA in writing of their actions.
The head-on collision of two Union Pacific trains at Devine, Texas, on June 22, indicated that direct train control procedures for issuing movement authorities should be changed.
